chunks: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-Muaddab (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: Ali ibn Salim said, on the authority of his father that I enquired from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (AS): “O son of the Messenger of Allah! What do you say about the Qur’an?”

Hence, he responded, “It is the Word of Allah, His Speech, His Book, the Revelation He revealed. It is the Honorable Book, which falsehood shall not come to it from before it not from behind it; a revelation from the Wise, the Praised One.”

key_terms.لَا يَأْتِيهِ الْبَاطِلُ: Falsehood shall not come to it

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of the Quran according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the Qur'an as the uncreated, literal Speech of Allah, a key tenet in Shia theology distinguishing it from created speech. By enumerating it as *Kalam*, *Qawl*, *Kitab*, and *Wahy*, he emphasizes its multifaceted divine nature, while the citation of Surah Fussilat 41:41 underscores its absolute purity from falsehood, reinforcing its status as the ultimate criterion for truth.
